one_line: Last great Shahi ruler of the Punjab frontier, who led a coalition against Mahmud of Ghazni near Chach c. 1008–1009 CE and was defeated, leaving the Hindu Shahis severely weakened and tributary.

appearance.age_look: Early 40s, tall and athletic with the solid build of an experienced cavalry commander.
appearance.face: Oval face with a strong jaw, medium-tan North Indian complexion, sharp straight nose, thick dark brows, and a neatly trimmed full mustache with short beard along the jawline; default expression calm but resolute, with focused, serious eyes.
appearance.hair: Long, straight black hair gathered into a low knot at the back of the head, partially covered by a deep-red turban wrapped in the early-medieval north Indian style, with a narrow gold band and a small central emerald-like stone at the forehead.
appearance.costume: Over a quilted, sleeveless cotton war-vest dyed muted indigo, he wears a long-sleeved, knee-length cotton tunic (angarkha-style overlap) in warm off-white with a subtle narrow red border at the cuffs and hem; a broad, deep-red cotton sash is wrapped firmly around his waist as a kamarband, holding a simple brown leather belt with a round bronze buckle; below, he wears loose, straight-cut churidar-style trousers in dull olive green gathered at the ankles, and sturdy brown leather riding boots reaching mid-calf; over one shoulder and across the chest is a light, ochre-colored woolen shawl/cloak suitable for the Punjab frontier climate, pinned with a small bronze brooch; minimal jewelry—only a pair of small gold hoop earrings and a single plain gold ring—keeps the look martial and practical.
appearance.signature: A slightly curved, single-edged steel sword (early talwar-like) with a plain bronze hilt and a worn brown leather scabbard, worn at his left hip and often held in his right hand as he gives commands.

ref_desc: Anandapala is a tall, early-40s North Indian king with a medium-tan oval face, mustache and short beard, long black hair in a knot under a deep-red turban, indigo quilted war-vest over an off-white tunic, olive trousers, brown boots, ochre shawl, and a plain-hilt curved steel sword at his left hip.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet of Anandapala, the early-medieval North Indian Shahi ruler: a tall, early-40s man with a medium-tan oval face, strong jaw, straight nose, thick dark brows, calm serious eyes, and a neatly trimmed mustache with short beard along the jawline. His long black hair is tied in a low knot at the back and partly covered by a deep-red turban wrapped in an early-medieval north Indian style, with a narrow gold band and a small green stone at the forehead. He wears a sleeveless, quilted cotton war-vest in muted indigo over a long-sleeved, knee-length off-white tunic that overlaps slightly at the chest, with a narrow red border at cuffs and hem. A broad deep-red cotton sash is tightly wrapped around his waist as a kamarband, over which sits a simple brown leather belt with a round bronze buckle. His trousers are loose, straight-cut olive-green churidar-style, gathered at the ankles, and he wears sturdy brown leather riding boots to mid-calf. A light ochre-colored woolen shawl or cloak is draped from one shoulder across his chest, pinned with a small bronze brooch, suggesting frontier chill. He has minimal jewelry—small gold hoop earrings and a single plain gold ring—to keep a martial, practical look. At his left hip hangs his signature weapon: a slightly curved single-edged steel sword with a plain bronze hilt and worn brown leather scabbard, which he holds in his right hand in some poses. Emphasize the deep-red, off-white, indigo, olive, and brown leather palette, and present him front, side, and back in consistent anime style, clearly showing face, hair, costume details, and sword.
